title: Economic Bulletin Issue 1, 2026
summary: The ECB Governing Council kept its three key interest rates unchanged at its 5 February 2026 meeting, with the deposit facility at 2.00%, main refinancing operations at 2.15%, and marginal lending facility at 2.40%. January 2026 inflation declined to 1.7% from 2.0% in December 2025, with core inflation (excluding energy and food) at 2.2%. The Governing Council reiterated it will follow a data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach and is not pre-committing to a particular rate path, while expressing concern about volatile global trade policy, geopolitical tensions, and uncertainties surrounding the euro area outlook.
key_points: ECB kept all three key interest rates unchanged: deposit facility at 2.00%, main refinancing operations at 2.15%, marginal lending facility at 2.40%
Euro area Q4 2025 GDP grew 0.3% (preliminary flash estimate), driven primarily by services with resilient manufacturing
Unemployment stood at 6.2% in December 2025, down from 6.3% in November 2025
January 2026 headline inflation fell to 1.7% from 2.0% in December; core inflation (excluding energy and food) was 2.2%
Bank lending rates for firms increased slightly to 3.6% in December 2025 from 3.5% in November; new mortgage rates held steady at 3.3%
Governing Council identifies global trade policy uncertainty and geopolitical tensions (particularly Russia's war against Ukraine) as major sources of risk to the outlook
why_it_matters: The ECB's decision to hold rates signals a cautious approach amid uncertainty, balancing benign inflation data (now at 1.7%) against risks from trade tensions and geopolitical developments. The Governing Council's insistence on data-dependency without forward commitment leaves markets without clear guidance on the timing or direction of next moves, creating uncertainty around the euro area rate path. Investors and policymakers need to monitor upcoming data releases to gauge whether the ECB remains on track for a possible rate cut or may need to maintain restrictive policy longer.
macro_context: The ECB continues to signal commitment to its 2% inflation target while acknowledging significant uncertainty. The balance sheet reduction continues as the Eurosystem no longer reinvests maturing securities. The euro area economy shows resilience with 0.3% Q4 growth and 6.2% unemployment, but faces headwinds from higher tariffs and a stronger euro reducing external demand. Growth support comes from defense and infrastructure spending, lower interest rates from prior cuts, and improving consumer confidence. Labor market remains supportive of incomes, though demand for labor has cooled.
